statements.text: Every dotfiles-ai full apply checks and converges the latest compatible stable OpenCode release on the host and all registered managed guests.
Use official OpenCode release assets and published SHA-256 digests on every platform; Homebrew formula state is not runtime authority.
Stage and validate one candidate everywhere before guest-then-host activation; rollback or durable commit recovery prevents fleet divergence.
Update activation never signals or restarts current OpenCode or Herdr processes; only later launches use the replacement inode.
A healthy fleet retains its verified release when metadata, download, validation, or a target is unavailable; unhealthy bootstrap and rollback failure remain nonzero.
Preserve OpenCode XDG state, sessions, providers, credentials, configuration, and current process state without inspection or copying across boundaries.
Validate version, help, resolved managed configuration, CLI role discovery, and required DBSCTR tool loading before activation.
OpenCode CLI/config contracts can drift on stable releases; incompatible candidates are rejected by canonical full-candidate digest and never activated.

Migrate Fedora guests from the delivered root-owned OpenCode binary to the user-local managed path; retain the root binary only as first-migration rollback authority and retire provisioning after fleet validation.

Migrate the host, every registered managed guest and supported provisioning and CI profiles to V2; the prior guest deferral is lifted for this migration, while additional unregistered machines remain excluded.
Include CLI and Desktop and qualify shared configuration, data, services and external-state-root behavior.

Use a separately approved controlled major-version migration window, preserving native conversation identity, provider affinity, worktree selection and writer authority; ordinary rolling updates retain their no-restart contract.
Prefer native V2 conversion with an immutable original archive and reviewed transformation report; retain existing recovery evidence and never discard post-cutover V2 work during rollback.
Report functional gaps with impact, safe unavailable behavior, owner and review condition for later reconciliation; perfect V1 feature parity is not required and no blanket gate exception is granted.
Unexplained message loss, incorrect authorization and unsafe recovery block activation; qualify native interfaces before declaring implementation readiness.
Retire V1 active launch, update, provisioning and CI paths after fleet verification; keep inactive recovery material until separately reviewed disposal without rewriting historical evidence.
Preserve boundary-local credentials and history throughout rehearsal and deployment; never copy host state into guests as an upgrade shortcut.
Extend this initiative using the approved lifecycle, OpenCode control-plane and distribution contexts; serialize shared ownership and preserve unrelated relocation work.

Provide a repeatable checksum-bound isolated V2 CLI surface probe with bounded subprocesses and sanitized results; surface success must never imply continuation, migration or deployment qualification.

Implement read-only V2 native actor and message-qualified terminal-proof compatibility from observed schema contracts; reject stale V1 fallback, incomplete conversion, ambiguous calls and background completion while preserving V1 and Codex regression behavior.
